arguments.content:
---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API to send and manage messages, read channel history, list and create channels, look up users, send direct messages, add reactions, and upload files. Use when Gemini CLI needs to post to Slack, automate Slack notifications, query a Slack workspace for channels, users, or messages, or perform any operation against Slack using an API token.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Enables interacting with a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API (`https://slack.com/api/`). Provides a reusable request script, a message-posting helper, and a reference for endpoints, payloads, scopes, and error handling.

## Prerequisites

- A Slack API token, from the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable or the `--token` flag:
  - Bot token (`xoxb-...`) for most automation
  - User token (`xoxp-...`) to act on behalf of a user
- The token must have the scopes required by the methods being called (see `references/api.md`).

## Quick Start

Post a message to a channel:

```bash
node scripts/post_message.cjs "#general" "Hello from an automated agent"
```

Call any Web API method:

```bash
node scripts/slack_request.cjs auth.test
node scripts/slack_request.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C123456","text":"Hello"}'
```

## Core Workflow

1. **Verify the token**: `node scripts/slack_request.cjs auth.test`
2. **Resolve names to IDs** (most methods require IDs): list channels with `conversations.list`, find users with `users.lookupByEmail` or `users.list`
3. **Perform the operation** with the appropriate method (see `references/api.md`)
4. **Check the response**: Slack returns `{"ok": true, ...}` on success and `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` on failure; scripts exit non-zero with a clean message on failure

## Scripts

### scripts/slack_request.cjs

Generic caller for any Slack Web API method. POSTs JSON to `https://slack.com/api/<method>`.

```bash
node scripts/slack_request.cjs <method> ['<json-body>'] [--token <token>]
```

Examples:

- `node scripts/slack_request.cjs auth.test`
- `node scripts/slack_request.cjs conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel","limit":100}'`
- `node scripts/slack_request.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C123456","text":"Hi","thread_ts":"1234.5678"}'`

Prints the JSON response to stdout (truncated if very large) and exits non-zero with a clean error message on failure. Requires Node.js 18+ (built-in `fetch`).

### scripts/post_message.cjs

Convenience wrapper for `chat.postMessage`.

```bash
node scripts/post_message.cjs <channel> <text> [--thread-ts <ts>] [--token <token>]
```

`<channel>` may be a channel ID (`C...`), a channel name (`#general`), or a user ID (`U...` for a direct message). Pass `--thread-ts` to reply inside a thread. Prints the message timestamp (`ts`) on success — store it for later updates, deletes, or reactions.

## Reference

Read `references/api.md` when you need:

- Endpoint reference with payloads and response shapes
- Scope requirements per method
- Pagination and rate-limit handling
- Error codes and troubleshooting
- Block Kit examples for rich message formatting

## Guidance

- **Prefer IDs over names** where possible; resolve names via `conversations.list` first.
- **Handle pagination**: list methods return `response_metadata.next_cursor`; pass it as `cursor` until empty.
- **Respect rate limits**: on HTTP 429, wait the seconds in the `Retry-After` header before retrying.
- **Never log or echo tokens**; pass them via `SLACK_TOKEN` or `--token` only.
- **Replies go in threads**: pass `thread_ts` to reply within a thread instead of sending a new top-level message.
- **Rich formatting uses Block Kit** JSON in the `blocks` field; plain `text` supports limited formatting.

# Slack Web API Reference

## Table of Contents

- [Authentication & Tokens](#authentication--tokens)
- [Common Patterns](#common-patterns)
- [Messaging](#messaging)
- [Conversations & Channels](#conversations--channels)
- [Users](#users)
- [Reactions](#reactions)
- [Files](#files)
- [Pagination](#pagination)
- [Rate Limits](#rate-limits)
- [Errors & Troubleshooting](#errors--troubleshooting)
- [Block Kit](#block-kit)

## Authentication & Tokens

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api/`
- All requests: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header
- Token types:
  - `xoxb-` bot token: acts as the bot, limited to granted scopes
  - `xoxp-` user token: acts on behalf of a user
- Get a token: create an app at https://api.slack.com/apps, add scopes (Bot Token Scopes), and install it to the workspace.
- Verify a token with `auth.test`; it returns `{"ok":true,"user_id":"U...","team_id":"T...","bot_id":"B..."}` or `{"ok":false,"error":"invalid_auth"}`.

## Common Patterns

### Resolve a channel name to an ID

Call `conversations.list` with `types=public_channel,private_channel`, paginate with `cursor`, and match on `name`. Use the returned `id` in later calls. Bots only see channels they have been added to.

### Send a message

`chat.postMessage` with `channel` (ID, `#name`, or user ID) and `text` and/or `blocks`.

### Send a direct message

1. `conversations.open` with `users` (comma-separated IDs) returns `channel.id`
2. `chat.postMessage` with that channel ID

### Reply in a thread

Pass `thread_ts` (the `ts` of the parent message) to `chat.postMessage`.

### Update / delete a message

`chat.update` requires `channel` + `ts` (plus new `text`/`blocks`). `chat.delete` requires `channel` + `ts`. Capture and store the `ts` from the original `chat.postMessage` response.

## Messaging

### chat.postMessage

Sends a message to a channel or DM.

Key params: `channel` (required), `text`, `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `reply_broadcast`, `link_names`, `mrkdwn`, `unfurl_links`.

Request:

```json
{"channel":"C123456","text":"Hello","link_names":true}
```

Response:

```json
{"ok":true,"channel":"C123456","ts":"1234567890.123456","message":{"type":"message","text":"Hello","ts":"1234567890.123456","channel":"C123456"}}
```

`ts` is the message identifier used for updates, deletes, replies, and reactions.

Common errors: `not_in_channel`, `channel_not_found`, `is_archived`, `invalid_auth`, `missing_scope`, `rate_limited`.

### chat.postEphemeral

Sends a message visible only to a specific user. Params: `channel`, `user`, `text`/`blocks`. Ephemeral messages cannot be updated or deleted later.

### chat.update

Params: `channel`, `ts`, `text`/`blocks`. Returns the updated message with a new `ts`.

### chat.delete

Params: `channel`, `ts`. Returns `{"ok":true,"channel":"C...","ts":"..."}`.

### chat.getPermalink

Params: `channel`, `message_ts`. Returns a `permalink` URL to the message.

### chat.scheduleMessage

Params: `channel`, `text`, `post_at` (Unix timestamp). Returns `scheduled_message_id`. Cancel with `chat.deleteScheduledMessage`.

## Conversations & Channels

### conversations.list

Lists channels the app can access. Params: `types` (`public_channel`, `private_channel`, `mpim`, `im`; comma-separated, default `public_channel`), `limit` (1-200, default 100), `cursor`, `exclude_archived`.

Response item: `{"id":"C...","name":"general","is_channel":true,"is_archived":false,"is_private":false,"num_members":12}`

### conversations.history

Fetches message history. Params: `channel`, `limit` (1-200), `cursor`, `oldest`/`latest` (Unix timestamps), `inclusive`.

Response: `{"ok":true,"messages":[...],"has_more":true,"response_metadata":{"next_cursor":"..."}}`

### conversations.replies

Fetches a message and its thread replies. Params: `channel`, `ts`.

### conversations.info

Gets channel info. Params: `channel`, `include_num_members`.

### conversations.create

Creates a channel. Params: `name` (lowercase, 1-80 chars), `is_private` (boolean). Returns the new channel. Common error: `name_taken`.

### conversations.invite

Params: `channel`, `users` (comma-separated IDs). Errors: `user_not_found`, `cant_invite_self`, `already_in_channel`.

### conversations.rename

Params: `channel`, `name`.

### conversations.archive / conversations.unarchive

Params: `channel`.

### conversations.open

Opens (and returns) a DM or multi-person DM. Params: `users` (comma-separated IDs) or `channel` (for MPIM). Returns `channel.id`, which you then use with `chat.postMessage`.

### conversations.members

Lists channel members. Params: `channel`, `limit`, `cursor`. Returns `members: ["U...", ...]`.

## Users

### users.lookupByEmail

Params: `email`. Returns `{"id":"U...","name":"...","real_name":"...","profile":{"email":"...","display_name":"..."}}`. Error: `users_not_found`.

### users.info

Params: `user`. Returns the full user object including `profile`.

### users.list

Lists all workspace users (paginable; may be large). Prefer `users.lookupByEmail` or `users.conversations` when possible.

### users.conversations

Lists channels/DMs the user is in. Params: `types`, `limit`, `cursor`.

## Reactions

### reactions.add

Params: `channel`, `name` (emoji without colons, e.g. `white_check_mark`), `timestamp` (message ts). Errors: `already_reacted`, `no_reaction`, `invalid_name`.

### reactions.remove

Params: `channel`, `name`, `timestamp`.

### reactions.get

Params: `channel`, `timestamp` (or `file`/`file_comment`). Returns the reactions on a message.

## Files

Modern upload flow (`files.upload` is deprecated):

1. `files.getUploadURLExternal` with `filename`, `length`, `alt_txt`, `snippet_type` → returns `upload_url` and `file_id`
2. Upload the file bytes to `upload_url` (not the Web API base URL); e.g. `curl -F file=@./report.pdf <upload_url>`
3. `files.completeUploadExternal` with `files: [{"id":"F...","title":"..."}]` → returns the uploaded `files` array

For simple text content, `files.upload` still works: params `channels` (comma-separated), `content` or `file` (multipart), `filename`, `initial_comment`, `title`.

## Pagination

- List methods return `response_metadata.next_cursor` when more results exist.
- Pass that value as `cursor` in the next request; repeat until `next_cursor` is empty.
- `limit` caps page size (max 200 for most list methods).

## Rate Limits

- Slack applies per-method rate tiers; HTTP 429 responses include a `Retry-After` header (seconds).
- On 429, wait `Retry-After` seconds before retrying; use exponential backoff for other transient errors.
- `x-ratelimit-*` response headers describe remaining capacity.

## Errors & Troubleshooting

Slack API errors return HTTP 200 with `{"ok": false, "error": "<code>"}`. Non-200 HTTP responses indicate network or auth-layer issues.

Common error codes:

| error | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` | Token is invalid or revoked |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks the required scope; check `needed` and `provided` fields |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot must be added to the channel first |
| `channel_not_found` | Channel ID is wrong or the app cannot see it |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived; unarchive before posting |
| `name_taken` | Channel name already exists |
| `rate_limited` | Slow down; honor `Retry-After` |
| `too_many_requests` | Global rate limit hit |
| `users_not_found` | Email/user does not match any member |
| `already_reacted` / `no_reaction` | Reaction already exists / does not exist |

Diagnostic tips:

- Run `auth.test` first to verify token validity.
- On `missing_scope`, add the scope listed in `needed` at https://api.slack.com/apps and reinstall the app.
- Use `conversations.info` to confirm the app can access a channel.
- Store the `ts` from `chat.postMessage` responses for later updates, deletes, and reactions.

## Block Kit

Rich messages use `blocks` (JSON array) instead of, or alongside, `text`. Common block types:

- `section`: `{"type":"section","text":{"type":"mrkdwn","text":"*Bold* and <https://example.com|a link>"}}`
- `divider`: `{"type":"divider"}`
- `header`: `{"type":"header","text":{"type":"plain_text","text":"Title"}}`
- `image`: `{"type":"image","image_url":"https://...","alt_text":"..."}`
- `actions` (buttons): `{"type":"actions","elements":[{"type":"button","text":{"type":"plain_text","text":"Click"},"action_id":"click","value":"1"}]}`
- `context`: small text under content

Example:

```json
{
  "channel": "C123456",
  "blocks": [
    {"type": "header", "text": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "Deploy finished"}},
    {"type": "section", "text": {"type": "mrkdwn", "text": "Build <https://ci.example.com|#42> succeeded in 3m 12s."}},
    {"type": "divider"},
    {"type": "actions", "elements": [{"type": "button", "text": {"type": "plain_text", "text": "View logs"}, "action_id": "logs", "url": "https://ci.example.com/logs"}]}
  ]
}
```

Notes: block `text` fields must specify `plain_text` or `mrkdwn` sub-type; maximum 50 blocks per message.
